text:
maria: Heads up — after rotating the org API key yesterday our long-running `rw stream` processes started getting 401s mid-run. Not seeing a restart in logs, just auth failures. Anyone seen this?

ken: hmm, we hit something like this a while back. Was the process started before you exported the new key? CLI flags should override env.

maria: yeah process started before rotation. We rotated via the console, updated `REDWOOD_API_KEY` in the shell but didn't restart the already-running streamer.

sophie: can you paste the exact command you used to start the stream and how you rotated keys? also which CLI version?

maria: `rw stream --app payments --mode live` (launched in screen). Rotation steps: console -> generate key -> `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_XXXXX` in my dev laptop shell. did not restart screen session. CLI is v1.12.3.

tim: this is expected technically — env vars are fixed at process start. two options: 1) restart processes or 2) implement in-process credential reloading (SIGHUP/SIGUSR1). we should also consider a long-lived credential provider daemon so background processes can fetch fresh creds without being restarted.

alex: we already have a small credential helper `redwood-cred-provider` used by some SDKs (talks to KMS / local cache). It listens on a unix socket. If we expose that as the default credential source for `rw` and sample apps, rotation becomes painless: the daemon picks up new keyfile and serves it.

sophie: proposal for env precedence (for clarity in docs): `--api-key` flag > `~/.redwood/credentials` file > `REDWOOD_API_KEY` env var > platform metadata. Also add scoped vars `REDWOOD_PROJECT` and `REDWOOD_ORG` for scoping when keys are project-level. Suggest default var names: `REDWOOD_API_KEY`, `REDWOOD_PROJECT`, `REDWOOD_ORG`.

ken: can we add an opt-in signal handler for the CLI and long-running tools so they call the provider reload or re-read file on `SIGHUP`? e.g., `export REDWOOD_RELOAD_ON_SIGHUP=true` and `kill -SIGHUP <pid>` in rotation scripts. :thumbsup:

sophie: love that. small UX note: document that interactive shells vs detached services behave differently. also add a shortcode example for systemd units:

```
# /etc/systemd/system/rw-stream.service
[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/rw stream --app payments
Environment=REDWOOD_API_KEY=/etc/redwood/secret.key
ExecReload=/bin/kill -HUP $MAINPID
```

(then `systemctl reload rw-stream` after updating the file)

alex: quick workaround for folks today: drop the new key into `~/.redwood/credentials` and `kill -SIGHUP $(pgrep rw)` for running `rw` processes. We'll follow up to make the provider the canonical source.

maria: thanks — that works for now. I'll add a note to the onboarding checklist about service restarts on rotation.

tim: I'll open GH issue: `cli: add credential provider + SIGHUP reload for long-running commands` and tag @sophie @alex to help design the UX and compat story with existing SDK credential chain. Will also propose env var names above.

maria: filing a small PR to docs after this convo with the `systemd` snippet.

deploy-bot: redeploy: rw-cli v1.12.3 promoted to stable @ 2025-11-02T09:12:00Z

ken: tiny follow-up — can we log an explanatory line when a 401 happens that includes which credential source was used (flag/file/env) without leaking the key? just `auth source: env` or `auth source: file` to help ops during rotation.

sophie: yes, add non-sensitive provenance logging. good call.

tim: thanks all. putting the GH issue and a short RFC on my plate. 

maria: thanks folks :pray:
